audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 10, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal witness and trade-history audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for the queen of Sheba's agency, intellectual exchange, court labor, royal spectacle, diplomatic gifts, exoticized trade, gold concentration, ivory, animals, militarization, Egyptian horse trade, and wisdom-versus-extraction tension.

verses.restored: Queen of Sheba heard report of Solomon concerning name of YHWH, and she came to test him with difficult questions.

familiar.text: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD, she came to prove him with hard questions.

modern.text: Now when the queen of Sheba heard about the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD, she came to test him with difficult questions.

original.text: וּמַֽלְכַּת שְׁבָ֗א שֹׁמַ֛עַת אֶת שֵׁ֥מַע שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה וַתָּבֹ֥א לְנַסֹּת֖וֹ בְּחִידֽוֹת

verses.restored: She came to Jerusalem with a very great company, camels carrying spices, very much gold, and precious stones. She came to Solomon and spoke with him all that was upon her heart.

familiar.text: And she came to Jerusalem with a very great train, with camels that bare spices, and very much gold, and precious stones: and when she was come to Solomon, she communed with him of all that was in her heart.

modern.text: She arrived in Jerusalem with a very large caravan—with camels bearing spices, gold in great abundance, and precious stones. So she came to Solomon and spoke to him all that was on her mind.

original.text: וַתָּבֹ֣א יְרוּשָׁלְַ֗מָה בְּחַיִל֮ כָּבֵ֣ד מְאֹד֒ גְּ֠מַלִּים נֹשְׂאִ֨ים בְּשָׂמִ֧ים וְזָהָ֛ב רַב מְאֹ֖ד וְאֶ֣בֶן יְקָרָ֑ה וַתָּבֹא֙ אֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וַתְּדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלָ֔יו אֵ֛ת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה עִם לְבָבָֽהּ

verses.restored: Solomon answered all her matters; no matter was hidden from king that he could not explain to her.

familiar.text: And Solomon told her all her questions: there was not any thing hid from the king, which he told her not.

modern.text: And Solomon answered all her questions; nothing was too difficult for the king to explain.

original.text: וַיַּגֶּד לָ֥הּ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה אֶת כָּל דְּבָרֶ֑יהָ לֹֽא הָיָ֤ה דָּבָר֙ נֶעְלָ֣ם מִן הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹ֦א הִגִּ֖יד לָֽהּ

verses.restored: Queen of Sheba saw all wisdom of Solomon and house he built,

familiar.text: And when the queen of Sheba had seen all Solomon’s wisdom, and the house that he had built,

modern.text: When the queen of Sheba saw all the wisdom of Solomon, the palace he had built,

original.text: וַתֵּ֨רֶא֙ מַֽלְכַּת שְׁבָ֔א אֵ֖ת כָּל חָכְמַ֣ת שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וְהַבַּ֖יִת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנָֽה

verses.restored: food of his table, seating of servants, attendance of ministers, their garments, cupbearers, and his ascent/burnt offering by which he went to house of YHWH; there was no more breath in her.

familiar.text: And the meat of his table, and the sitting of his servants, and the attendance of his ministers, and their apparel, and his cupbearers, and his ascent by which he went up unto the house of the LORD; there was no more spirit in her.

modern.text: the food at his table, the seating of his servants, the service and attire of his attendants and cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he presented at the house of the LORD, it took her breath away.

original.text: וּמַאֲכַ֣ל שֻׁלְחָנ֡וֹ וּמוֹשַׁ֣ב עֲבָדָיו֩ וּמַעֲמַ֨ד משרתו וּמַלְבֻּֽשֵׁיהֶם֙ וּמַשְׁקָ֔יו וְעֹ֣לָת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲלֶ֖ה בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹא הָ֥יָה בָ֛הּ ע֖וֹד רֽוּחַ

verses.restored: She said to king, True was word I heard in my land concerning your words/deeds and wisdom.

familiar.text: And she said to the king, It was a true report that I heard in mine own land of thy acts and of thy wisdom.

modern.text: She said to the king, “The report I heard in my own country about your words and wisdom is true.

original.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֱמֶת֙ הָיָ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי בְּאַרְצִ֑י עַל דְּבָרֶ֖יךָ וְעַל חָכְמָתֶֽךָ

verses.restored: I did not believe words until I came and my eyes saw. Look, half was not told me; your wisdom and prosperity exceed report I heard.

familiar.text: Howbeit I believed not the words, until I came, and mine eyes had seen it: and, behold, the half was not told me: thy wisdom and prosperity exceedeth the fame which I heard.

modern.text: But I did not believe these things until I came and saw with my own eyes. Indeed, not even half was told to me. Your wisdom and prosperity have far exceeded the report I heard.

original.text: וְלֹֽא הֶאֱמַ֣נְתִּי לַדְּבָרִ֗ים עַ֤ד אֲשֶׁר בָּ֨אתִי֙ וַתִּרְאֶ֣ינָה עֵינַ֔י וְהִנֵּ֥ה לֹֽא הֻגַּד לִ֖י הַחֵ֑צִי הוֹסַ֤פְתָּ חָכְמָה֙ וָט֔וֹב אֶל הַשְּׁמוּעָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמָֽעְתִּי

verses.restored: Happy are your people/men; happy are these your servants who continually stand before you and hear your wisdom.

familiar.text: Happy are thy men, happy are these thy servants, which stand continually before thee, and that hear thy wisdom.

modern.text: How blessed are your men! How blessed are these servants of yours who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom!

original.text: אַשְׁרֵ֣י אֲנָשֶׁ֔יךָ אַשְׁרֵ֖י עֲבָדֶ֣יךָ אֵ֑לֶּה הָֽעֹמְדִ֤ים לְפָנֶ֨יךָ֙ תָּמִ֔יד הַשֹּׁמְעִ֖ים אֶת חָכְמָתֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Blessed be YHWH your Divine, who delighted in you to place you upon throne of Israel. Because YHWH loved Israel forever, YHWH made you king to do justice and righteousness.

familiar.text: Blessed be the LORD thy God, which delighted in thee, to set thee on the throne of Israel: because the LORD loved Israel for ever, therefore made he thee king, to do judgment and justice.

modern.text: Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delighted in you to set you on the throne of Israel. Because of the LORD’s eternal love for Israel, He has made you king to carry out justice and righteousness.”

original.text: יְהִ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ בָּר֔וּךְ אֲשֶׁר֙ חָפֵ֣ץ בְּךָ֔ לְתִתְּךָ֖ עַל כִּסֵּ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל בְּאַהֲבַ֨ת יְהוָ֤ה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְעֹלָ֔ם וַיְשִֽׂימְךָ֣ לְמֶ֔לֶךְ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָֽה

verses.restored: She gave king one hundred twenty talents of gold, very great abundance of spices, and precious stones. Never again came such abundance of spices as Queen of Sheba gave King Solomon.

familiar.text: And she gave the king an hundred and twenty talents of gold, and of spices very great store, and precious stones: there came no more such abundance of spices as these which the queen of Sheba gave to king Solomon.

modern.text: Then she gave the king 120 talents of gold, a great quantity of spices, and precious stones. Never again was such an abundance of spices brought in as those the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.

original.text: וַתִּתֵּ֨ן לַמֶּ֜לֶךְ מֵאָ֥ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֣ים כִּכַּ֣ר זָהָ֗ב וּבְשָׂמִ֛ים הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹ֖ד וְאֶ֣בֶן יְקָרָ֑ה לֹא בָא֩ כַבֹּ֨שֶׂם הַה֥וּא עוֹד֙ לָרֹ֔ב אֲשֶׁר נָתְנָ֥ה מַֽלְכַּת שְׁבָ֖א לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹֽה

verses.restored: Hiram's fleet that brought gold from Ophir also brought from Ophir very great amounts of almug wood and precious stones.

familiar.text: And the navy also of Hiram, that brought gold from Ophir, brought in from Ophir great plenty of almug trees, and precious stones.

modern.text: (The fleet of Hiram that brought gold from Ophir also brought from Ophir a great cargo of almug wood and precious stones.

original.text: וְגַם֙ אֳנִ֣י חִירָ֔ם אֲשֶׁר נָשָׂ֥א זָהָ֖ב מֵאוֹפִ֑יר הֵבִ֨יא מֵאֹפִ֜יר עֲצֵ֧י אַלְמֻגִּ֛ים הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹ֖ד וְאֶ֥בֶן יְקָרָֽה

verses.restored: King made from almug wood supports for house of YHWH and king's house, and lyres and harps for singers. Such almug wood had not come or been seen until this day.

familiar.text: And the king made of the almug trees pillars for the house of the LORD, and for the king’s house, harps also and psalteries for singers: there came no such almug trees, nor were seen unto this day.

modern.text: The king made the almug wood into steps for the house of the LORD and for the king’s palace, and into lyres and harps for the singers. Never before had such almug wood been brought in, nor has such been seen to this day.)

original.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ אֶת עֲצֵ֨י הָאַלְמֻגִּ֜ים מִסְעָ֤ד לְבֵית יְהוָה֙ וּלְבֵ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְכִנֹּר֥וֹת וּנְבָלִ֖ים לַשָּׁרִ֑ים לֹ֣א בָֽא כֵ֞ן עֲצֵ֤י אַלְמֻגִּים֙ וְלֹ֣א נִרְאָ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: King Solomon gave Queen of Sheba all her desire, whatever she asked, besides what he gave her according to royal hand. She turned and went to her land, she and her servants.

familiar.text: And king Solomon gave unto the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatsoever she asked, beside that which Solomon gave her of his royal bounty. So she turned and went to her own country, she and her servants.

modern.text: King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba all she desired—whatever she asked—besides what he had given her out of his royal bounty. Then she left and returned to her own country, along with her servants. Solomon’s Wealth and Splendor (2 Chronicles 1:14–17; 2 Chronicles 9:13–28)

original.text: וְהַמֶּ֨לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה נָתַ֣ן לְמַֽלְכַּת שְׁבָ֗א אֶת כָּל חֶפְצָהּ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁאָ֔לָה מִלְּבַד֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָֽתַן לָ֔הּ כְּיַ֖ד הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וַתֵּ֛פֶן וַתֵּ֥לֶךְ לְאַרְצָ֖הּ הִ֥יא וַעֲבָדֶֽיהָ

verses.restored: Weight of gold coming to Solomon in one year was six hundred sixty-six talents of gold,

familiar.text: Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred threescore and six talents of gold,

modern.text: The weight of gold that came to Solomon each year was 666 talents,

original.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ מִשְׁקַ֣ל הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥א לִשְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בְּשָׁנָ֣ה אֶחָ֑ת שֵׁ֥שׁ מֵא֛וֹת שִׁשִּׁ֥ים וָשֵׁ֖שׁ כִּכַּ֥ר זָהָֽב

verses.restored: besides from traders, merchant traffic, all kings of Arabia, and governors of land.

familiar.text: Beside that he had of the merchantmen, and of the traffick of the spice merchants, and of all the kings of Arabia, and of the governors of the country.

modern.text: not including the revenue from the merchants, traders, and all the Arabian kings and governors of the land.

original.text: לְבַד֙ מֵאַנְשֵׁ֣י הַתָּרִ֔ים וּמִסְחַ֖ר הָרֹכְלִ֑ים וְכָל מַלְכֵ֥י הָעֶ֖רֶב וּפַח֥וֹת הָאָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold; six hundred shekels of gold went upon each shield.

familiar.text: And king Solomon made two hundred targets of beaten gold: six hundred shekels of gold went to one target.

modern.text: King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold; six hundred shekels of gold went into each shield.

original.text: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה מָאתַ֥יִם צִנָּ֖ה זָהָ֣ב שָׁח֑וּט שֵׁשׁ מֵא֣וֹת זָהָ֔ב יַעֲלֶ֖ה עַל הַצִּנָּ֥ה הָאֶחָֽת

verses.restored: He made three hundred small shields of hammered gold; three minas of gold went upon each shield. King placed them in House of Forest of Lebanon.

familiar.text: And he made three hundred shields of beaten gold; three pound of gold went to one shield: and the king put them in the house of the forest of Lebanon.

modern.text: He also made three hundred small shields of hammered gold; three minas of gold went into each shield. And the king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.

original.text: וּשְׁלֹשׁ מֵא֤וֹת מָֽגִנִּים֙ זָהָ֣ב שָׁח֔וּט שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת מָנִים֙ זָהָ֔ב יַעֲלֶ֖ה עַל הַמָּגֵ֣ן הָאֶחָ֑ת וַיִּתְּנֵ֣ם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ בֵּ֖ית יַ֥עַר הַלְּבָנֽוֹן

verses.restored: The king made a great throne of ivory and overlaid it with refined gold.

familiar.text: Moreover the king made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with the best gold.

modern.text: Additionally, the king made a great throne of ivory and overlaid it with pure gold.

original.text: וַיַּ֧עַשׂ הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ כִּסֵּא שֵׁ֖ן גָּד֑וֹל וַיְצַפֵּ֖הוּ זָהָ֥ב מוּפָֽז

verses.restored: The throne had six steps, a rounded top behind, arms on both sides of seat, and two lions standing beside arms.

familiar.text: The throne had six steps, and the top of the throne was round behind: and there were stays on either side on the place of the seat, and two lions stood beside the stays.

modern.text: The throne had six steps, and its back had a rounded top. There were armrests on both sides of the seat, with a lion standing beside each armrest.

original.text: שֵׁ֧שׁ מַעֲל֣וֹת לַכִּסֵּ֗ה וְרֹאשׁ עָגֹ֤ל לַכִּסֵּה֙ מֵאַֽחֲרָ֔יו וְיָדֹ֛ת מִזֶּ֥ה וּמִזֶּ֖ה אֶל מְק֣וֹם הַשָּׁ֑בֶת וּשְׁנַ֣יִם אֲרָי֔וֹת עֹמְדִ֖ים אֵ֥צֶל הַיָּדֽוֹת

verses.restored: Twelve lions stood there upon six steps, one on each side. Nothing like it was made for any kingdom.

familiar.text: And twelve lions stood there on the one side and on the other upon the six steps: there was not the like made in any kingdom.

modern.text: Twelve lions stood on the six steps, one at either end of each step. Nothing like this had ever been made for any kingdom.

original.text: וּשְׁנֵ֧ים עָשָׂ֣ר אֲרָיִ֗ים עֹמְדִ֥ים שָׁ֛ם עַל שֵׁ֥שׁ הַֽמַּעֲל֖וֹת מִזֶּ֣ה וּמִזֶּ֑ה לֹֽא נַעֲשָׂ֥ה כֵ֖ן לְכָל מַמְלָכֽוֹת

verses.restored: All King Solomon's drinking vessels were gold, and all vessels of House of Forest of Lebanon were pure gold; silver was considered as nothing in days of Solomon.

familiar.text: And all king Solomon’s drinking vessels were of gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were of pure gold; none were of silver: it was nothing accounted of in the days of Solomon.

modern.text: All King Solomon’s drinking cups were gold, and all the utensils of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. There was no silver, because it was accounted as nothing in the days of Solomon.

original.text: וְ֠כֹל כְּלֵ֞י מַשְׁקֵ֨ה הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה֙ זָהָ֔ב וְכֹ֗ל כְּלֵ֛י בֵּֽית יַ֥עַר הַלְּבָנ֖וֹן זָהָ֣ב סָג֑וּר אֵ֣ין כֶּ֗סֶף לֹ֥א נֶחְשָׁ֛ב בִּימֵ֥י שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לִמְאֽוּמָה

verses.restored: King had a fleet of Tarshish at sea with Hiram's fleet. Once in three years fleet came bearing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks/baboons.

familiar.text: For the king had at sea a navy of Tharshish with the navy of Hiram: once in three years came the navy of Tharshish, bringing gold, and silver, ivory, and apes, and peacocks.

modern.text: For the king had the ships of Tarshish at sea with Hiram’s fleet, and once every three years the ships of Tarshish would arrive bearing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.

original.text: כִּי֩ אֳנִ֨י תַרְשִׁ֤ישׁ לַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ בַּיָּ֔ם עִ֖ם אֳנִ֣י חִירָ֑ם אַחַת֩ לְשָׁלֹ֨שׁ שָׁנִ֜ים תָּב֣וֹא אֳנִ֣י תַרְשִׁ֗ישׁ נֹֽשְׂאֵת֙ זָהָ֣ב וָכֶ֔סֶף שֶׁנְהַבִּ֥ים וְקֹפִ֖ים וְתֻכִּיִּֽים

verses.restored: King Solomon became greater than all kings of earth in riches and wisdom.

familiar.text: So king Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth for riches and for wisdom.

modern.text: So King Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.

original.text: וַיִּגְדַּל֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה מִכֹּ֖ל מַלְכֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ לְעֹ֖שֶׁר וּלְחָכְמָֽה

verses.restored: All earth sought face of Solomon to hear wisdom Divine had put in his heart.

familiar.text: And all the earth sought to Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.

modern.text: The whole world sought an audience with Solomon to hear the wisdom that God had put in his heart.

original.text: וְכָ֨ל הָאָ֔רֶץ מְבַקְשִׁ֖ים אֶת פְּנֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה לִשְׁמֹ֨עַ֙ אֶת חָכְמָת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁר נָתַ֥ן אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּלִבּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Each brought gift: vessels of silver and gold, garments, weapons, spices, horses, and mules, a yearly amount.

familiar.text: And they brought every man his present, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and garments, and armour, and spices, horses, and mules, a rate year by year.

modern.text: Year after year, each visitor would bring his tribute: articles of silver and gold, clothing, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.

original.text: וְהֵ֣מָּה מְבִאִ֣ים אִ֣ישׁ מִנְחָת֡וֹ כְּלֵ֣י כֶסֶף֩ וּכְלֵ֨י זָהָ֤ב וּשְׂלָמוֹת֙ וְנֵ֣שֶׁק וּבְשָׂמִ֔ים סוּסִ֖ים וּפְרָדִ֑ים דְּבַר שָׁנָ֖ה בְּשָׁנָֽה

verses.restored: Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen. He had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, stationed in chariot cities and with king in Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And Solomon gathered together chariots and horsemen: and he had a thousand and four hundred chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he bestowed in the cities for chariots, and with the king at Jerusalem.

modern.text: Solomon accumulated 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses, which he stationed in the chariot cities and also with him in Jerusalem.

original.text: וַיֶּאֱסֹ֣ף שְׁלֹמֹה֮ רֶ֣כֶב וּפָרָשִׁים֒ וַיְהִי ל֗וֹ אֶ֤לֶף וְאַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת֙ רֶ֔כֶב וּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֖לֶף פָּֽרָשִׁ֑ים וַיַּנְחֵם֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י הָרֶ֔כֶב וְעִם הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: King made silver in Jerusalem like stones, and cedars like sycamores in lowland for abundance.

familiar.text: And the king made silver to be in Jerusalem as stones, and cedars made he to be as the sycomore trees that are in the vale, for abundance.

modern.text: The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as abundant as sycamore in the foothills.

original.text: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ אֶת הַכֶּ֛סֶף בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם כָּאֲבָנִ֑ים וְאֵ֣ת הָאֲרָזִ֗ים נָתַ֛ן כַּשִּׁקְמִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר בַּשְּׁפֵלָ֖ה לָרֹֽב

verses.restored: Solomon's horses were imported from Egypt and Kue; king's merchants acquired them from Kue at a price.

familiar.text: And Solomon had horses brought out of Egypt, and linen yarn: the king’s merchants received the linen yarn at a price.

modern.text: Solomon’s horses were imported from Egypt and Kue; the royal merchants purchased them from Kue.

original.text: וּמוֹצָ֧א הַסּוּסִ֛ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִשְׁלֹמֹ֖ה מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וּמִקְוֵ֕ה סֹחֲרֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יִקְח֥וּ מִקְוֵ֖ה בִּמְחִֽיר

verses.restored: A chariot came up and went out from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for one hundred fifty. Thus through their hand they exported them to all kings of Hittites and kings of Aram.

familiar.text: And a chariot came up and went out of Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and an horse for an hundred and fifty: and so for all the kings of the Hittites, and for the kings of Syria, did they bring them out by their means.

modern.text: A chariot could be imported from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty. Likewise, they exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and to the kings of Aram.

original.text: וַֽ֠תַּעֲלֶה וַתֵּצֵ֨א מֶרְכָּבָ֤ה מִמִּצְרַ֨יִם֙ בְּשֵׁ֣שׁ מֵא֣וֹת כֶּ֔סֶף וְס֖וּס בַּחֲמִשִּׁ֣ים וּמֵאָ֑ה וְ֠כֵן לְכָל מַלְכֵ֧י הַחִתִּ֛ים וּלְמַלְכֵ֥י אֲרָ֖ם בְּיָדָ֥ם יֹצִֽאוּ

translation_notes: The queen of Sheba is a sovereign intellectual and diplomatic actor who travels with resources, questions Solomon, evaluates his court, blesses YHWH, negotiates exchange, and returns to her own country.
Her astonishment includes servants, ministers, food, dress, architecture, and ritual. Court magnificence depends upon extensive labor and disciplined hierarchy.
Her blessing names justice and righteousness as the purpose of kingship; wealth and reputation are not the standard.
Spices, gold, gems, rare wood, ivory, animals, horses, and textiles come through long-distance networks involving extraction, animal capture, transport danger, and workers absent from the narrative.
The ivory throne requires killed elephants or traded tusks; animal bodies are part of royal spectacle.
Gold shields and vessels convert extreme wealth into display while silver loses value at court. Abundance concentrated at the center does not prove equitable prosperity.
Apes and other animals brought as exotic cargo should not be romanticized; capture and transport likely involved suffering.
Chariot and horse accumulation conflicts with Torah's warnings about royal militarization and return to Egypt.
The chapter intentionally moves from a woman praising justice to an inventory of excess, inviting the reader to test Solomon's wisdom against his accumulation.
safety_note: Do not exoticize the queen of Sheba, erase her sovereignty, or reduce her to admiration of a male king. Do not present ivory, captured animals, gold concentration, tribute, or arms trading as uncomplicated blessing. Measure wisdom by justice and righteousness.
